raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4-Flash PD on A3 fails when prefill runs without speculation and decode enables DSpark. The target C4 compressor uses an 8-row ring on P and a 16-row ring on D. A3 currently bundles each entire attention/indexer ring into the SWA state component, so the peers publish different item strides:

- Attention state: 65,536 vs 131,072 bytes (8,192 bytes per row).
- Indexer state: 16,384 vs 32,768 bytes (2,048 bytes per row).

The shared manager correctly rejects this layout mismatch, and generation returns HTTP 500 with the Ascend transfer backend. This PR addresses that original failure only.

## Modifications

The diff is limited to **three production files and one regression-test file**. C4 payload construction stays in the existing hook; no request-pool API is added.

- Keep A3 SWA registration limited to SWA KV pages; register C4 attention/indexer state as individual rows through the existing Ascend C4 component.
- Derive the last eight logical history positions independently on each peer, using its request token table, full-to-SWA mapping and local ring size. This follows the A3 explicit compressor table, including history spanning noncontiguous SWA pages.
- Keep the existing A5 request-bank mapping and the shared stride/index-length guards.
- Add regression coverage for short histories, ring/page boundaries, different physical page mappings, row-sized registration, and agreement with the actual compressor history table.

Both P and D must use the updated A3 state layout. There is no mixed-version wire compatibility. Separate PP empty-component and ROCm unified-state issues are outside this PR.

## Accuracy Tests

On main `ad6ca42dea36ffad53fa033dab400f40ffa677f7` plus this patch:

- Six `TestC4StateTransferLayout` tests passed with real production-module imports at compact revision `3ae39491` in the Ascend environment (torch 2.10.0+cpu / torch_npu 2.10.0.post6, CANN 9.1). The current cleanup is covered by the CPU sender/consumer and 1,020 before/after checks below; no new device or full-model run is claimed.
- A separate CPU harness passes 10 checks and 420 bounds-checked byte-transfer cases through the extracted production sender and consumer methods. Coverage includes 8-to-16, 16-to-8, equal-ring and 8-to-32 transfers, short histories, ring/page boundaries, and untouched destination rows. Import/allocation/network boundaries are doubled in this harness.
- Ruff 0.15.1 formatting and selected lint checks, isort 7, AST parsing and `git diff --check` pass.

Hardware regression was performed on the original reported base `93f4f1a87dbf356833e5d2ec777ee4b006b631fd` plus the same runtime fix:

- Real two-process/two-NPU MemFabric SDMA: 32 transfer cases match byte-for-byte; 128 A3 compressor output comparisons match an independently populated reference state. This uses real pools and allocator with synthetic nonidentity page tables and weights.
- Full DeepSeek-V4-Flash W8A8 PD on Ascend 910C: P without speculation, D with DSpark gamma 5 / verify width 6; TP16 / attention DP16 per side, PP1, BF16 KV, radix cache disabled. **28/28 requests return HTTP 200**, producing 1,344 output tokens with speculative verification observed on every request. Cases include prompt lengths around 128/256/512 and two rounds of eight concurrent requests with slot reuse.
- The hardware-tested registration, sender, stride checks and compressor history table are retained. C4 index construction now lives in the existing payload hook: 1,020 before/after A3/A5 comparisons match exactly across 8/16/32-row rings, distinct physical pages, short/page-boundary histories and negative-length normalization. The full-model run was not repeated on this compact revision.

These are state-correctness and functional-serving checks; they do not establish full-model task accuracy. Hardware coverage is PP1.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance claim. The request regression is not a throughput or latency benchmark.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code and check imports.
- [x] Add focused unit tests.
- [x] Document the two-peer upgrade requirement above.
- [x] Report functional/state correctness results and their coverage limits.
